bull_bear.body: Priority: INR750cr net debt reduction in FY27; then strategic business development (land acquisition, JDA); no dividend guidance; cash balance of INR1,695cr as of Mar'26 supports flexibility
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body: Geopolitical uncertainty impacting NRI demand; regulatory delays in approvals (esp. Bengaluru); construction cost inflation; execution risk in large redevelopment projects (Malabar Hills, Chembur); commercial leasing velocity may lag projections
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: Confident, disciplined, and forward-looking; strong emphasis on balance sheet health, premiumization, and execution capability; transparent on challenges (approval delays) but optimistic on demand resilience; no overpromising on timelines
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body: INR600cr+ interest expense includes fair-value accounting for equity-linked debt (NCDs), not just cash interest; Starworth’s INR2,000cr+ order book is unconsolidated but material; Malabar Hills pricing at INR115k-120k/sq.ft implies ultra-premium positioning; 35M sq.ft land bank remains after FY27 pipeline execution
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- Net debt of ₹2,836 Cr with net debt/equity rising to 1.57x (from 1.31x in Q4 FY26) as the company stepped up land acquisitions and capex; cost of debt was 11.12% in Q1 FY27.
- Total estimated surplus potential of ₹19,831 Cr over the next 3–5 years (₹8,976 Cr from ongoing projects + ₹8,636 Cr from the launch pipeline + ₹2,220 Cr from commercial projects), which management states is sufficient to cover total debt obligations including ₹1,410 Cr of "payable when able" NCDs.
- Debt repayment is front-loaded: 25% due within 1 year and 41% in year 2, with balance receivables from already-sold units (₹6,708 Cr) covering ~72% of the balance cost to complete.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

business.body: Residential: 7.25M sq.ft sold in FY26, avg realization INR10,213/sq.ft; Commercial: Zentech (44% leased/sold), Aerocity (leasing underway), Thane retail (3L sq.ft); Redevelopment: Chembur (1.2M sq.ft, GDV INR2,100cr), Malabar Hills (0.7M sq.ft, GDV INR2,700cr); Plotted: margins 35-40%; New launches: Purva Northern Lights (INR1,100-1,200cr Q4 presales, INR10,700/sq.ft), Purva Estrella (INR800cr+ presales, >20% margin)
business.title: Segment / subsidiary detail

business.body:
- 50 years of legacy with 97 completed projects across 9 cities, 59 msft of delivered area, and a brand narrative built on trust, quality and execution excellence ("Building Spaces. Enriching Lives.").
- Actively diversifying away from its Bengaluru core: ~41% of Q1 FY27 sales volume came from outside Bengaluru (vs 50% in Q1 FY26), with Chennai's share of sales value rising from 15% to 17%.
- Building a distinct Mumbai redevelopment franchise — 7 projects (Estrella, Deccan, Apna Ghar 3, Malabar Hill, Deonar Baug, Miami, Cuffe Parade) totalling 5.49 msft developable / 3.14 msft saleable area (Puravankara's share).
business.title: Positioning (investor deck)

business.body:
- [Governance/Shareholding] Promoter and promoter-group holding is 75.00% and fully unencumbered as of 30 June 2026; FPIs hold 16.62%, including Atyant Capital India Fund I, Gothic Corporation and Vanderbilt University.
- [Recognition] 145+ media stories in leading print/digital outlets during the period, plus multiple 2025–26 industry awards (Pride of India 2025, CIDC Vishwakarma Achievement Award, British Safety Council International Safety Award 2026 for Provident Deansgate).
- [Share price] PURVA stock fell 28.15% over the trailing 12 months (01-Jul-25 to 30-Jun-26), underperforming both the Sensex (-8.61%) and the BSE Realty index (-15.91%) despite the operational growth narrative.
business.title: Notable from the deck

latest_quarter.body: Q4 EBITDA margin 22% (up from 12% in FY25); premium projects yield 20-21% gross margins; redevelopment projects target 20%+; plotted projects 35-40%; construction costs up 6-7% due to diesel, but mitigated by pricing power and contingencies
latest_quarter.title: Margins & cost dynamics

outlook.body: revenue growth: INR11,200cr presales target for FY27 (+51% YoY); margin: sustained 20%+ EBITDA margins expected across premium launches; order inflow: 48% from existing portfolio, 52% from new launches; capex/commissioning: INR750cr debt reduction target (excl. strategic BD), no explicit capex guidance but land acquisition and project development funded via incremental debt and cash flow
outlook.title: Guidance

themes.title: Real-estate up-cycle - premium housing & redevelopment
themes.need: The residential up-cycle is now presales-led with a visible margin cost. SOBHA posted its highest-ever presales at INR 3,656cr (+76% YoY, 2.34 msf at an average INR 15,655/sqft, NCR at a record INR 1,384cr) and guided FY27 presales at +30% or better - but reported EBITDA is still only ~9.7%, guided to 17-20% only by exit-Q4, and forthcoming-project marginal cash flow was cut from ~INR 86bn to INR 68.3bn on a heavier joint-development mix. SUNTECK booked INR 787cr of presales (+20%) with ZERO launches in the quarter, with aspirational-luxury (Naigaon/Kalyan) at 21% of presales 'picking up because of the lower interest rate' - the first sign the rate-elastic end is turning on demand rather than inventory release. DLF's FY26 bookings of INR20,143cr and 50mn sq ft of rental at 95% occupancy anchor the annuity leg; LODHA/GODREJPROP/PRESTIGE-tier and MMR redevelopers (RUSTOMJEE, KALPATARU, RAYMONDREL, MANINFRA, SURAJEST) ride premiumization; PHOENIXLTD/EMBDL on mixed-use.
themes.driver: SOBHA's exit-Q4 margin ramp from ~9.7% to 17-20% is the falsifiable claim (JD-heavy growth structurally lowers marginal margins); rate-elastic aspirational absorption (SUNTECK); FY27 launch-pipeline execution and festive booking momentum.
